records.verificationNote: Read directly off the 'Anticoagulants – Oral' subsection (VIII. Hematological Agents, page 42) of the NYRx PDP Preferred Drug List PDF, revised/effective 2026-07-16 (date printed on every page header). Confirmed verbatim: Preferred column lists 'dabigatran capsule', 'Eliquis®', 'warfarin', 'Xarelto® tablet' (tagged DO for Dose Optimization), and 'Xarelto® 2.5 mg tablet' (tagged BLTG); Non-Preferred column lists 'Eliquis® sprinkle, packets', 'Pradaxa® pellet pack, capsule', 'rivaroxaban tablet, suspension (gen Xarelto®)', 'Savaysa®', and 'Xarelto® dose pack, suspension'. The document's general rule (page 4) states non-preferred drugs require PA unless indicated otherwise, and preferred drugs needing PA are footnoted with a superscript — no such footnote appears on any of the five preferred DOAC-class entries, so preferredRestriction is confirmed null. No step-therapy criterion is listed for this drug class in either the PDL section or the separate DUR Step-Therapy table (pages 62-75), so stepTherapy is confirmed null. The apixaban strength (5 mg BID) and sig are inferred (standard FDA-labeled AFib/VTE dosing), not read verbatim from the PDL, since this is a coverage list, not a dosing reference — apixaban (Eliquis) was selected as the representative preferred agent because it is the guideline-preferred first-line DOAC for stroke prevention in AFib (best bleeding-risk profile, no INR monitoring), even though dabigatran, warfarin, and rivaroxaban (Xarelto) are equally 'preferred, no PA' on this same PDL and are listed under alternatives. No tier/copay-level statement is made anywhere in this section beyond the binary Preferred/Non-Preferred PA status itself, which functions as NYRx's only cost-tier mechanism for this fee-for-service program. Because NY carved pharmacy benefits out of Medicaid managed care into this single statewide FFS NYRx PDL effective 2023-04-01, this same PDL and PA determination applies to every NY Medicaid MCO (Healthfirst, Fidelis, MetroPlus, etc.), confirmed by the document's own framing (page 1) that the PDP applies uniformly to 'NYRx, the Medicaid Pharmacy Program'.

Page 4 gives the abbreviation key (MS/PA/PV/QL/S/ST) and the 3-tier definitions (Tier 1 = most cost-effective generics, Tier 2 = preferred brand with clinical/value advantage, Tier 3 = all other brand/generic, often with more cost-effective alternatives). Page 83 lists the 'DIRECT FACTOR XA INHIBITORS' section verbatim: ELIQUIS (Tier 2, QL;PV), ELIQUIS DVT-PE TREAT 30D START (Tier 2, QL;PV), ELIQUIS SPRINKLE (Tier 2, QL;PV), rivaroxaban generic (Tier 1, QL;PV), XARELTO (Tier 2, QL;PV), XARELTO DVT-PE TREAT 30D START (Tier 2, PV). Page 85 lists 'THROMBIN INHIBITOR - SELECTIVE DIRECT AND REVERSIBLE': dabigatran etexilate generic (Tier 3, QL;PV). A full-document keyword scan across all 144 extracted pages found zero occurrences of 'apixaban' as a standalone generic line (only the ELIQUIS brand line exists — no generic apixaban entry on this formulary as of the 9/1/2026 revision, despite generic apixaban being FDA-approved and on the market) and zero occurrences of 'edoxaban' or 'savaysa' anywhere in the document, confirming edoxaban is non-formulary. Pages 4-5 give the tier legend (Tier 1 = lowest cost, Tier 2 = mid-range, Tier 3 = highest) and the symbol key, including 'E' = 'May be excluded from coverage or subject to Prior Authorization in Connecticut, New Jersey and New York' - directly relevant since this record is for the NY footprint. Page 11's 'Anticoagulants - Drugs to Treat or Prevent Blood Clots' section was read verbatim and lists exactly nine lines relevant here: dabigatran etexilate mesylate (Tier 2, QL), ELIQUIS TABLET (Tier 2, QL), jantoven (Tier 1), PRADAXA ORAL CAPSULE (Tier E, QL), rivaroxaban (Tier 2, QL), warfarin sodium oral (Tier 1), and XARELTO (Tier 2, QL) - plus two non-DOAC anticoagulants (enoxaparin/LOVENOX) excluded from this record. Directly verified: apixaban is listed only as brand ELIQUIS (no generic apixaban line anywhere in the document, consistent with generic apixaban not yet having launched in the US as of this Jan 2026 effective date under ongoing patent-settlement exclusivity), at Tier 2 with only a quantity limit (no PA/step) - this is the basis for choosing it as the preferred agent (also the most commonly prescribed, guideline-favored DOAC nationally) and for genericAvailable:false and preferredRestriction:null. Also directly verified: both the rivaroxaban generic and brand XARELTO sit at the identical Tier 2/QL, so no brand-over-generic tier steering is evidenced (boglActive:false); dabigatran's brand PRADAXA carries the 'E' flag (excluded/PA in NY) while its generic is clean Tier 2. The one INFERRED (not directly confirmed) data point is edoxaban/Savaysa: it does not appear anywhere in the document, and since the PDL states it covers only 'the most commonly prescribed medications' rather than every approved drug, its absence is treated as non-formulary but this is an inference from silence, not a read PA-criteria statement - hence overall verification is 'partial' rather than 'verified' despite the preferred-agent data being read verbatim with the effective date visible.
